source.title: REEF: Representation Encoding Fingerprints for Large Language Models
source.authors: Jie Zhang; Dongrui Liu; Chen Qian; Linfeng Zhang; Yong Liu; Yu Qiao; Jing Shao

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures representation similarity and presents evidence that high similarity tracks shared model lineage, while models trained from scratch on different data can have low similarity. It also examines sensitivity to inputs and similarity settings, refining the scope of convergence claims.
record.gate_note: The paper measures CKA similarity between representations of the same samples. Included are CKA results for derived, unrelated, pruned, merged, permuted, and scaled models, plus stated results on kernels, sample counts, and datasets. Classifier accuracies, weight/logit baselines, and cited findings are not rows because they do not measure representation-distance convergence itself.
record.test_reason: A fingerprinting paper, but it reports linear CKA between independently trained 7B LLMs (unrelated models, and same-architecture models trained from scratch on different data). These values are low (mean 0.2361; below 0.2 at large n), which bears on whether independent models' representations align (V7). It also reports how the measured similarity varies with kernel, sample count and dataset (V6). Derived-model results reflect shared weights, not convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that CKA-based REEF separates models derived from a victim from unrelated ones (0.9585 vs 0.2361 mean). It stays robust to fine-tuning up to 700B tokens, pruning up to 90%, merging, permutation and scaling, and evading it via fine-tuning destroys model capability. They add that same-architecture models trained on different data, and different model generations, show low similarity, and that the separation gap depends on dataset, with TruthfulQA best.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses representation CKA as a model-lineage fingerprint, rather than testing convergence with scale or capability. It compares a linear and an RBF kernel, but does not provide a scale/performance convergence experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The derived-versus-unrelated similarity gap varies across datasets (approximately 0.8 on TruthfulQA and about 0.5 on ToxiGen). Similarities for most models stabilize after 200-300 samples. Linear and RBF kernels are reported to give similar results.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear, MLP, CNN and GCN probes trained on Llama-2-7b/13b representations transfer to fine-tuned descendants at ~70-80% accuracy, with no mapping, but fall to ~50% (chance) on unrelated models (Section 3, Appendix B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept probes trained on one model do not transfer without a mapping to independently trained models, though they do to fine-tuned descendants.

fits_no_version.finding: Representations of fine-tuned, pruned (up to 90%) and merged descendants keep CKA >0.93 with the base model, even after 700B tokens of fine-tuning. Adversarial fine-tuning that reduces this similarity destroys language ability (Appendix D, OPT-1.3B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning preserves base-model representation geometry; lineage dominates representation similarity.

record.problems: The experiments are designed for model fingerprinting, not scale- or capability-related convergence; they use Llama-2-7b as the main victim and do not isolate the causal role of shared data or objectives. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Several comparisons are described from figures without numeric values. The paper notes that empirical validation beyond 700B fine-tuning tokens is lacking.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No size or capability sweep of independently trained models. All unrelated comparisons are at roughly 7B scale.
No vision-language or paired image-caption comparison.
No same-architecture, same-data, different-seed comparison. Openllama and Amber differ in data as well as initialisation.
No mapping, stitching, or relative-representation tests. The classifier transfer in Section 3 applies probes directly without any mapping.
No interpretable features or circuits compared.
No mutual-nearest-neighbour metrics or neighbour counts, and no out-of-distribution inputs. Only two CKA kernels were compared.
No test of a scale plateau. Shared data and shared objectives are not separated by design; the distillation-merge evidence is incidental.

missing.what: Per-model CKA values for unrelated models (Mistral, Qwen, Baichuan, Falcon, MPT, Internlm2) individually, and under the RBF kernel
Per-dataset unrelated-model similarity curves (SST2, ConfAIde, PKU-RLHF, ToxiGen) vs sample count, including Openllama-2-7b and Falcon-7b
Numeric CKA for Openllama-7b, Amber, Llama-3-8b and Internlm pairs

record.verdict_notes: The paper is about model fingerprinting; its relevance to convergence is incidental. The key evidence is that independently trained ~7B LLMs have low linear CKA (~0.2) on the same inputs, even with the same architecture. Most rows (derived, permuted, scaled, weight-merged) reflect shared weights or mathematical invariance and are relinked to none. The distillation-merge reading for V7 is our inference, not the authors'. This is a single-layer and single-scale setting, and most unrelated-model values are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep tests whether representation alignment rises as independently trained models get larger or more capable.
No comparison of same-architecture networks trained from different random initializations.
CKA similarity is measured, but the paper does not test mapping representations between models, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are identified across models.
The paper examines linear versus RBF kernels, sample counts, and selected datasets, but does not test different neighbor counts or out-of-distribution inputs.
The study examines model lineage, fine-tuning, mergers, and different pretraining data, but does not isolate shared objectives or data from other causes, nor measure a scale-related plateau.

relationships.reason: Unrelated models' CKA with Llama-2-7b averages 0.2361, is 0.2223 at layer 18, and falls below 0.2 with more samples. Same-architecture scratch-trained and cross-generation pairs are described as low (R2, R7, R38, R44-R47).
